title: Assembly files
description: How a set's assembly tables are written — which columns, in what order, under what headings, how a side and a unit are said —: data, a section of the settings tree each plugin that makes such files declares. The plain set has its own (settings/plugin/gerber/assembly, KiCad's columns); a pcb house brings its own and the same writer writes it (AssemblyTables).

$schema.description: the schema this file is written to

placement.description: The placement table: one line a seated part, where it stands and how it is turned.

file.description: what its file is called after the set's name: pos.csv is -pos.csv

role.description: what it is, as the set's README says it

sides.description: how each side is said: top → Top; a side not named is said as it is

unit.description: written after every length: mm, or nothing

mountings.description: how each way a part is mounted is said: surface → SMD; a way not named is said as it is

items.description: A column: its heading, and the field it shows — designator, value, footprint, component, x, y, rotation, side, designators, quantity, item (the line's number), mounting (surface or through-hole, by its pads), or meta:, a line of the component's own head (meta:lcsc).

heading.description: what the column is headed with

field.description: what it shows, by the field's word

materials.description: The bill of materials: one line a kind of part, its designators together.

file.description: what its file is called after the set's name: bom.csv is -bom.csv

role.description: what it is, as the set's README says it

designatorSeparator.description: what stands between a line's designators: " ", ","
